title: Shop Small: Our Favorite Gifts From Independent Businesses
gist: Gift guide for Small Business Saturday (November 28) highlighting 11 independent shops such as Yoseka Stationery, Heath Ceramics and Crown Northampton. Little investable content; the main framing is that independent retailers compete with Amazon and Walmart on curation and specialization, alongside slow-fashion and buy-it-for-life craftsmanship themes.

insights.claim: WIRED argues small independent businesses compete with Amazon and Walmart not on convenience but on curation and specialization, offering expert guidance that mass-market sites with millions of listings do not.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Curation and expertise remain the defensible niche for small retail against marketplace scale.
insights.quote: small, independent businesses offer some critical things the big guys don’t: curation and specialization.
insights.locator: We get it—Ordering from Amazon is easy.

insights.claim: Brooklyn's Kai D Utility is described as part of a growing slow-fashion movement selling handmade garments meant to last a lifetime, while Crown Northampton makes made-to-order boots with zero outsourcing as a fifth-generation family business dating to 1908.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Durability and provenance are being marketed as premium attributes in apparel and footwear.

insights.claim: Heath Ceramics, founded in 1948, still makes its original dinnerware, vases and tiles, which WIRED says are fully back in style due to midcentury modern design trends.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Minor consumer-taste signal: midcentury modern heritage design remains in demand.
insights.locator: A Vase for Your Best Bud
